BACK-471 - Fix cli-commit-behaviour tests using git rev-list --count HEAD

Replace git rev-list --all --count with git rev-list --count HEAD in
getCommitCountInTest. The --all flag includes refs/notes/ai commits
created asynchronously by the global git-ai trace2 tool, inflating
counts non-deterministically. HEAD-scoped counting matches the approach
in cli.test.ts and correctly measures commits on the current branch.

fix: sort milestones ascending by ID in browser UI

Previously the milestones page sorted milestone cards by ID descending
(newest first), so a project with phases m-3 through m-6 would display
Phase 9 (m-6) at the top, followed by Phase 7 (m-4) and Phase 8 (m-5).

This reverses the sort to ascending so milestones appear in their natural
creation order (m-1 → m-2 → m-3 … ), matching the sequence users intend
when they create milestones in phase/sprint order.

feat: add ordinal as sortable column in list view

The task list view (web UI + CLI) previously only supported sorting by
id and priority. Tasks have an ordinal field used for manual wave-based
ordering, which the board view already respects — but the list view
ignored it entirely, showing tasks in ID order with no way to recover
the deliberate sequence.

Changes:
- TaskList.tsx: add "ordinal" to TaskSortColumn union type; add ordinal
  sort case in sortedDisplayTasks useMemo (tasks with ordinals come
  first, then ascending by ordinal value, matching board view behavior);
  add sortable "Ordinal" column header and data cell in the table
- cli.ts: add "ordinal" to validSortFields in all four task list/draft
  list call sites; update --sort option help text accordingly

Closes #643

BACK-494 - Backlog-Guard: PreToolUse hook to enforce MCP/CLI access to backlog dirs

Adds hooks/backlog-guard/ — a hard-blocking PreToolUse hook that intercepts
Read/Edit/Write/Bash operations on files inside configured backlog directories
and redirects the agent to the correct MCP tool or CLI command.

Config via .backlog-guard YAML at git root (auto-discovered via git rev-parse);
falls back to auto-detecting backlog/config.yml in the directory tree. Block
messages include the exact MCP call and CLI command, with task ID extracted from
the filename (back-NNN-title.md) for task files.

Also adds .codex/skills/backlog-guard-setup/SKILL.md — a setup skill that
auto-detects the backlog directory, creates .backlog-guard, writes the hook entry
into the appropriate settings file, and optionally adds mcp__backlog__* allowlist
entries.

SHA-pin release.yml actions, disable shellcheck in actionlint, set sonar.python.version

- release.yml: SHA-pin all actions (checkout v6.0.2, cache v5.0.5, setup-bun v2.2.0,
  setup-node v5, upload-artifact v7.0.1, download-artifact v4, gh-release v2,
  git-auto-commit v5, harden-runner v2.19.3)
- Upgrade softprops/action-gh-release v1 -> v2 (fixes Node.js 16 deprecation)
- Upgrade stefanzweifel/git-auto-commit-action v4 -> v5
- Add FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24=true to release.yml
- Add step-security/harden-runner on ubuntu-latest jobs
- Disable shellcheck in actionlint (-shellcheck=) to avoid info-level
  warnings in release.yml causing exit code 1
- Add sonar.python.version=3 to suppress SonarQube Python version warning

Fix ShellCheck warnings in release.yml, re-enable shellcheck in actionlint

- SC2086/SC2016: Rewrite jq package.json generation to use --arg instead
  of shell interpolation, eliminating unquoted variable warnings
- SC2016: Add shellcheck disable comments for node -e template literals
- SC2012: Replace 'ls -lh' with 'stat' for binary size reporting in
  github-release job
- Remove '-shellcheck=' flag from actionlint step since all shellcheck
  findings are now resolved

Fix SC2016 properly: split node -e into separate calls instead of shellcheck disable

Replace single-line node -e with template literals by splitting into
two node -e calls for platform and arch, concatenated by the shell.
This eliminates the false-positive SC2016 (shell thinks ${} in JS
template literals are shell variables).

Merge pull request #4 from lenucksi/fix/actionlint-shellcheck-sonarpython

(newest first), so a project with phases m-3 through m-6 would display
Phase 9 (m-6) at the top, followed by Phase 7 (m-4) and Phase 8 (m-5).

when they create milestones in phase/sprint order.

Read/Edit/Write/Bash operations on files inside configured backlog directories
and redirects the agent to the correct MCP tool or CLI command.

Config via .backlog-guard YAML at git root (auto-discovered via git rev-parse);
falls back to auto-detecting backlog/config.yml in the directory tree. Block
messages include the exact MCP call and CLI command, with task ID extracted from
the filename (back-NNN-title.md) for task files.

Also adds .codex/skills/backlog-guard-setup/SKILL.md — a setup skill that
auto-detects the backlog directory, creates .backlog-guard, writes the hook entry
into the appropriate settings file, and optionally adds mcp__backlog__* allowlist
entries.

Phase 9 (m-6) at the top, followed by Phase 7 (m-4) and Phase 8 (m-5).

This reverses the sort to ascending so milestones appear in their natural
creation order (m-1 → m-2 → m-3 … ), matching the sequence users intend
when they create milestones in phase/sprint order.

id and priority. Tasks have an ordinal field used for manual wave-based
ordering, which the board view already respects — but the list view
ignored it entirely, showing tasks in ID order with no way to recover
the deliberate sequence.

Read/Edit/Write/Bash operations on files inside configured backlog directories
and redirects the agent to the correct MCP tool or CLI command.

Config via .backlog-guard YAML at git root (auto-discovered via git rev-parse);
falls back to auto-detecting backlog/config.yml in the directory tree. Block
messages include the exact MCP call and CLI command, with task ID extracted from
the filename (back-NNN-title.md) for task files.

Also adds .codex/skills/backlog-guard-setup/SKILL.md — a setup skill that
auto-detects the backlog directory, creates .backlog-guard, writes the hook entry
into the appropriate settings file, and optionally adds mcp__backlog__* allowlist
entries.

fix: sort milestones ascending by ID in browser UI

Previously the milestones page sorted milestone cards by ID descending
(newest first), so a project with phases m-3 through m-6 would display
Phase 9 (m-6) at the top, followed by Phase 7 (m-4) and Phase 8 (m-5).

This reverses the sort to ascending so milestones appear in their natural
creation order (m-1 → m-2 → m-3 … ), matching the sequence users intend
when they create milestones in phase/sprint order.

BACK-494 - Backlog-Guard: PreToolUse hook to enforce MCP/CLI access to backlog dirs

Adds hooks/backlog-guard/ — a hard-blocking PreToolUse hook that intercepts
Read/Edit/Write/Bash operations on files inside configured backlog directories
and redirects the agent to the correct MCP tool or CLI command.

Config via .backlog-guard YAML at git root (auto-discovered via git rev-parse);
falls back to auto-detecting backlog/config.yml in the directory tree. Block
messages include the exact MCP call and CLI command, with task ID extracted from
the filename (back-NNN-title.md) for task files.

Also adds .codex/skills/backlog-guard-setup/SKILL.md — a setup skill that
auto-detects the backlog directory, creates .backlog-guard, writes the hook entry
into the appropriate settings file, and optionally adds mcp__backlog__* allowlist
entries.

fix: make listDocuments fail loudly instead of silently returning empty array

The try/catch wrapper in listDocuments() swallowed all errors (including
YAML parse failures from spec files) and returned an empty array silently.
This caused 'backlog spec list' to show 'No specs found' even when 25
valid spec files existed, just because 3 files had broken YAML frontmatter.

Remove the try/catch wrapper so parse errors propagate to the caller
with full stack traces, enabling users to identify and fix root causes.

Fix backlog-jira pull integration bugs

Fixed four critical issues preventing Jira pull from working:

1. Database column name mismatch - SQLite returns snake_case (jira_key)
   but code expected camelCase (jiraKey). Updated getMapping() methods
   to transform column names properly.

2. MCP response format mismatch - Expected nested 'fields' property but
   MCP Atlassian returns flat structure. Updated jira_get_issue parsing
   to handle flat response with summary/status at top level.

3. Missing issue_type field - Made optional with default "Task" since
   MCP doesn't return it by default.

4. SQL parameter mismatch - updateSyncState() needed values duplicated
   for both INSERT and UPDATE clauses in UPSERT query.

Also added debug logging and fixed environment variable mapping to use
JIRA_EMAIL or JIRA_USERNAME interchangeably.

BACK-462 - Server: workspace REST API + persisted current pointer

Adds the workspace surface to BacklogServer:

- GET    /api/workspaces           — list registered + currentId
- POST   /api/workspaces           — register a new path (auto-init if empty)
- PATCH  /api/workspaces/:id       — switch current; persists to yml
- DELETE /api/workspaces/:id       — remove from registry

The PATCH handler swaps core.filesystem.rootDir AND writes `current`
to workspaces.yml so the selection survives server restarts (the
launchd-managed service relies on this — its plist runs `backlog
server` with no --project, and the resolver reads `current` on boot).

A workspaceMutationLock serializes PATCH/DELETE against each other
in-process so a delete can't race a switch and remove the workspace
that just became active. File-level mutation is already serialized
via withWriteLock in workspaces-index.

fix(ids): Ensure IDs for new items increment correctly

Previously, the ID generation for new tasks, documents, and decisions was unreliable. This was because the logic depended on parsing existing filenames, which did not always contain the full ID, causing new items to often be created with a non-incremented ID like `...-1`.

This change fixes the issue by adopting the ID normalization pattern from upstream for documents and decisions. This robustly formats the IDs before creating filenames, which allows the ID generation logic to correctly scan for the highest existing ID and increment it properly.

End-to-end tests have been added to verify that creating new tasks, documents, and decisions via the CLI results in correctly incremented IDs.

fix(cli): respect autoCommit setting for all commands

This change ensures that all commands that create or modify files, such as creating tasks, documents, or decisions, now correctly respect the `autoCommit` setting in the project's `config.yml`.

- The `Core` methods now consistently check the configuration before performing a git commit.
- End-to-end tests have been added using `Bun.spawnSync` to verify the behavior for both `autoCommit: true` and `autoCommit: false` scenarios.

feat(ids): Add support for zero-padded IDs

This introduces a new configuration option, `zeroPaddedIds`, to enable consistent formatting for task, document, and decision IDs.

When `zeroPaddedIds` is set to a number greater than 0 in `config.yml`, all newly generated IDs will be left-padded with zeros to the specified length. For example, with `zeroPaddedIds: 3`, the first task will be `task-001`.

This feature provides several benefits:
- Ensures consistent lexicographical sorting of files in the file system.
- Improves readability in lists and Kanban boards.
- Aligns with common conventions in issue tracking systems.

Key Changes:
- Updated `generateNextId`, `generateNextDocId`, and `generateNextDecisionId` in `src/cli.ts` to incorporate the padding logic.
- Sub-task IDs are now padded to a fixed length of 2 digits (e.g., `task-001.01`).
- Added `zeroPaddedIds` to the configuration handling in `src/file-system/operations.ts`.
- Introduced new e2e tests in `src/test/cli-zero-padded-ids.test.ts` to validate the feature.
- Updated `README.md` to document the new configuration option.

BACK-465 - Detect and warn about duplicate task IDs in web, TUI, and MCP interfaces

When two git branches independently create tasks with the same numeric ID
and are then merged, the duplicate is silently dropped. This adds detection
and user-facing warnings across all three surfaces:

- Web browser: amber dismissible banner listing duplicate groups with a
  "Copy AI fix prompt" button that provides a ready-to-use prompt
- TUI board: 15-second startup warning in the footer listing affected IDs
- MCP task_list: prepends a ⚠️ warning block with the AI cleanup prompt

Detection runs against the raw filesystem task list (before Map dedup)
so duplicates aren't lost before they can be reported.

fix(draft): set promoted task status to defaultStatus

Closes #624.

When a draft is promoted to a task, the file-system layer copied the
draft straight through with its existing "Draft" status. Once moved
out of the drafts directory, that status no longer matched any column
on the kanban board, so promoted tasks were invisible unless the user
manually added a "Draft" column or edited the task afterwards. Both
the in-memory promotion path (Backlog.promoteDraftWithUpdates ->
saveTask) and the kanban serialization treat "Draft" as a magic
draft-only marker, so leaving it on a non-draft is incorrect.

Set the promoted task's status to `config.defaultStatus` (falling
back to FALLBACK_STATUS = "To Do", same default used elsewhere in
core/backlog.ts), so the new task lands in the first kanban column
and is immediately visible.

BACK-414 - Document running backlog browser as a background service

## Summary
- add a "Running as a Service" section to README.md covering three OS
  recipes for keeping `backlog browser --no-open` alive and auto-starting
  on boot: systemd user unit (Linux/WSL2), launchd LaunchAgent (macOS),
  and Scheduled Task or NSSM (Windows)
- add a cross-reference note in CLI-INSTRUCTIONS.md pointing to the new
  section from the Web Interface table

The `--no-open` flag on `backlog browser` is ideal for running the web
UI as a background service, but the README/CLI docs never walked users
through that shape. Users who wanted a persistent backlog dashboard
either had to keep a terminal open or roll their own unit file.

Add Windows shell support to status-change callbacks

The onStatusChange hook previously hardcoded `sh -c`, which failed silently
on Windows hosts without Git Bash. Adds an optional `shell` field to
backlog.config.yml (`auto` | `sh` | `bash` | `cmd` | `pwsh` | `powershell`

current POSIX behavior, and on Windows prefers sh.exe when present (Git
for Windows ships one) with a one-time warning fallback to cmd.exe.

  executeStatusCallback; module-level warnedOnce for the cmd.exe fallback.

Fix drag-and-drop between kanban columns when target column is shorter than source

The TaskColumn root div used min-h-* but not h-full, so it only grew
to fit its content. In both flexbox (All Tasks) and CSS Grid (Milestone)
layouts, the wrapper divs stretch to match the tallest sibling, but the
TaskColumn inside did not fill its wrapper. When dragging from the bottom
of a long column, the cursor was below the shorter target column's DOM
boundary, so onDragOver/onDrop events never fired.
